key_insight: QSITE uses an exact sine filter to approximate imaginary-time evolution, with sequential and coherent implementations that prepare the same state with identical success probability.
engineering_relevance: QSITE offers two ground-state preparation designs with different resource and probability-boosting requirements: ancilla-reusing sequential LCU circuits and coherent QSVT circuits.
method: Concatenate linear combinations of unitaries, reusing two ancillas through mid-circuit measurement.
Implement the equivalent filter coherently using quantum singular value transformation.
Prove convergence to ideal imaginary-time evolution and identify favorable evolution-time zones for MaxCut.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulations of random Erdős–Rényi MaxCut instances up to 24 qubits, benchmarking against QAOA, and a bound keeping failure probability below 1/2 under specified error and timing conditions.
watch_item: The MaxCut failure bound is conditional, and the abstract does not establish hardware performance or an advantage over QAOA.
paper_title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
